features.description: L1 PRs are one-shot immutable snapshots; commits added after creation never join the PR, and no pr.update event exists. Any review-fix loop needs follow-up commits on the same change: devflow fix rounds send a worker back into the SAME worktree/branch; with immutable snapshots every round must recreate the PR and re-collect approve + ci.check, so review history fragments across N PRs for one logical change. A pr.update event re-pins the PR to the branch tip as a NEW snapshot generation; existing immutability is kept per generation.
expectedBehavior: `pr update <n>` re-pins the PR to the branch tip; event body records old/new source_head/base_head/merge_base
Each update is addressable as a new immutable generation; generation-0 L1 refs unchanged
`pr show` exposes the latest generation; diff = merge_base..latest source_head
Approve-before-update cannot merge post-update content (gate refuses pre-update approve/CI)
After update, fresh approve + fresh CI green on the latest generation merges
dogfood gains update-then-merge assertions (stale approve refused, fresh approve passes)

features.description: git forge pr merge refuses when refs/heads/<base> has moved since pr create; the only remedy is recreating the PR. Multiple in-flight PRs against the same base serialize — the moment one merges, every other PR is stale. Agent pipelines land feature branches one after another onto a moving integration branch, so recreate churn is per-merge, not exceptional. Live-base merge recomputes merge_base against the current base tip and binds review/CI to the merge result.
expectedBehavior: Two PRs on one base: first merges; second's base moved → merge refuses (no re-validation)
After fresh CI run + fresh approve (result-bound), the second PR's live-base merge passes
Finalize CASes the CURRENT base tip the gate validated (F-007/F-008 binding redesign named in code)
CAS conflict injected (base moved between gate validation and finalize): merge fails, refs unchanged, no partial write
dogfood gains two-PR live-base assertions (refuse without fresh gate, pass with)

features.description: every Forge Event actor is the repo user.email; in the single-user local setting the orchestrator, the implementing subagent, and the reviewing subagent all share one identity — the Review gate proves 'an approve event exists', not 'someone other than the implementer approved'. The wire contract should say so, and a future multi-agent pipeline wants role attribution in the chain. Identity resolution shells out to `git -C <worktree> config`, so per-worktree identity is already technically reachable via extensions.worktreeConfig or GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0/GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 env overrides — but neither is a promised interface.

steps.command: cargo test (exit zero) + dogfood role-attribution assertions

expectedBehavior: Three roles (worker/reviewer/orchestrator) produce distinguishable event actors in one repo
Per-worktree identity via extensions.worktreeConfig works and is documented
Environment override (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT etc.) works and is documented
Wire contract (docs/architecture/git-forge.md + mirror) declares the role semantics
Review gate: an approve from the implementer's own role does not satisfy 'someone other than the implementer approved' (when roles are distinct)
